title: ANCHOR-Grid: Authenticating Smart Grid Digital Twins Using Real World Anchors
content: Integrating digital twins (DTs) into smart grid systems within the Internet of Smart Grid Things (IoSGT) ecosystem presents both security challenges and novel opportunities. Advanced Deepfake technologies enable adversaries to create highly realistic yet fraudulent DTs, threatening critical infrastructures’ reliability, safety, and integrity. In this paper, we introduce Authenticating Networked Computerized Handling of Representations for Smart Grid security (ANCHOR-Grid), a novel authentication framework that leverages Electric Network Frequency (ENF) signals as real-world anchors to secure smart grid DTs against Deepfake attacks. By capturing distinctive ENF variations from physical grid components and embedding these environmental fingerprints into their digital counterparts, ANCHOR-Grid provides a robust mechanism to ensure the authenticity and trustworthiness of virtual representations. We conducted comprehensive simulations and experiments within a virtual smart grid environment to evaluate ANCHOR-Grid. We crafted both authentic and Deepfake DTs of grid components, with the latter attempting to mimic legitimate behavior but lacking correct ENF signatures. Our results show that ANCHOR-Grid effectively differentiates between authentic and fraudulent DTs, demonstrating its potential as a reliable security layer for smart grid systems operating in the IoSGT ecosystem. These findings highlight the importance of integrating real-world environmental data into authentication processes for critical infrastructure and lay the foundation for future research on leveraging physical-world cues to secure digital ecosystems.
